E1.evidence: Issue #103 (corot, 2013-10-16) states the concrete defect: "On 3dsensor.launch, depthimage_to_laserscan looks for depth/image_raw topic, but if we are using depth_registration (the default behavior) it will not work because in this case depth image topic is depth_registered/image_raw." Maintainer jihoonl closed it with: "https://github.com/turtlebot/turtlebot/commit/3e32933c829e308600707a9f971334d13d1cbe19 should have resolved this issue."

E2.evidence: The two units interact through a topic whose name is bound in turtlebot_bringup/launch/3dsensor.launch. At the parent revision b26d199a the launch file set `<arg name="depth_registration" default="true"/>` and wired the consumer with `<remap from="image" to="$(arg camera)/depth/image_raw"/>`. The fix 3e32933 (only file changed: turtlebot_bringup/launch/3dsensor.launch) adds `<arg     if="$(arg depth_registration)" name="depth" value="depth_registered" />` / `<arg unless="$(arg depth_registration)" name="depth" value="depth" />` and changes the remaps to `<remap from="image" to="$(arg camera)/$(arg depth)/image_raw"/>`. The name mismatch crosses the boundary, but the minimal resolving change only rebinds a topic remap in the launch file; neither depthimage_to_laserscan's nor openni_launch's declared interface changed. Stop at step 3: deployment_wiring. Other material: commenter robinJKU links https://github.com/ros-drivers/openni_launch/issues/7 (no depth images at all with depth registration on, attributed to the openni driver), a separate composition not addressed by this fix.

E3.evidence: PAIR: depth images published by the openni pipeline feed depthimage_to_laserscan's image input ("depthimage_to_laserscan starves if depth_registration is true").

E4.evidence: Issue title "depthimage_to_laserscan starves if depth_registration is true" and body "it will not work": the consumer receives no images (no data).

ineligible_reason: deployment_wiring: the fix only changes launch-file topic remaps (turtlebot_bringup/launch/3dsensor.launch) to follow the depth_registration argument; no unit's declared interface changed.
